senses.gloss: Māla, pl. (ºāḥ), a people. § 574 (Jambūkh.): VI, 9, 347 (in Bhāratavarsha).
Mālā, a river. § 276 (Jarāsandhavadhap.): II, 20, 795 (crossed by Kṛshṇa, Bhīmasena, and Arjuna on their way from Indraprastha to Girivraja).

Malla, pl. (ºāḥ), a people. § 280 (Bhīmasena): II, 30, 1077 (ºānām adhipaṃ, vanquished by Bhīmasena, in the east), 1086 (dakshiṇa-Mºān, in the east, vanquished by Bhīmasena). --§ 549 (Pāṇḍavapraveśap.): IV, 1, 12.--§ 574 (Jambūkh.): VI, 9, 354. Cf. Mallarāshṭra.
malla, pl. (ºāḥ) (“athletes”): II, 102; IV, 339 foll.; IX, 1231; XIV, 2039.
Malada, pl. (ºāḥ), a people. § 280 (Bhīmasena): II, 30, 1082 (in the east, vanquished by Bhīmasena on his digvijaya). --§ 589 (Droṇābhishekap.): VII, 7, 183 (followed Duryodhana and Karṇa).
Malaja, pl. (ºāḥ), a people. § 574 (Jambūkh.): VI, 9, 353 (only B., C. has Malayāḥ).
Mālatikā, a mātṛ. § 615u (Skanda): IX, 46, 2622.

Mālava, pl. (ºāḥ), a people. § 285 (Nakula): II, 32, 1189 (in the west, vanquished by Nakula on his digvijaya).-§ 287 (Rājasūyikap.): II, 34, 1270 (came to the rājasūya of Yudhishṭhira).--§ 295 (Dyūtap.): II, 52, 1871 (brought tribute to Yudhishṭhira, Kshudraka-Mºāḥ).--§ 342 (Indralokābhigamanap.): III, 51, 1991 (had been present at the rājasūya of Yudhishṭhira).--§ 515 (Karṇadigvijaya): III, 254, 15256 (vanquished by Karṇa on his digvijaya).--§ 545 (Pativratāmāhātmyap.): III, 297, 16807 (hundred M. shall be begotten by Aśvapati on his wife Mālavī).--§ 561 (Yānasandhip.): V, 57, 2249 (the M. and the Śālvakas are assigned to the Kekayas as their matches in the battle). --§ 574 (Jambūkh.): VI, 9, 367 (only B., C. has Mālavānakāḥ), 370 (in the south).--§ 578 (Bhīshmavadhap.): VI, 51, 2106 (Kshudraka-Mºaiḥ, in the army of Duryodhana). --§ 580 (do.): VI, 59, †2584 (Kshudraka-Mºāḥ, attacked Arjuna) (), †2646 (Kshudraka-Mºāḥ, defeated by Arjuna). --§ 585 (do.): VI, 87, 3852 (in the van of the army of Duryodhana), (), 3853 (Kshudraka-Mºāḥ).--§ 586 (do.): VI, 106, 4808 (defended Bhīshma, cf. v. 5649).--§ 587 (do.): VI, 117, 5484 (attacked Arjuna); 119, 5649 (saṃgrāmeṇa jahur Bhīshmaṃ, B.; saṃgrāme nājahuḥ, etc., C.).--§ 589 (Droṇābhishekap.): VII, 7, 183 (followed Duryodhana and Karṇa); 11, 398 (formerly vanquished by Kṛshṇa).--§ 592 (Saṃśaptakavadhap.): VII, 19, 768 (among the Saṃśaptakas who are slain by Arjuna).--§ 595 (Shoḍaśarāj., v. Rāma Jāmadagnya): VII, 70, 2435 (Kshudraka-Mºān, had been slain by Rāma Jāmadagnya).-§ 600 (Ghaṭotkacavadhap.): VII, 157, 6948, 6950 (slain by Yudhishṭhira); 161, 7206 (do.) (), 7208 (slain by Arjuna).--§ 604 (Karṇap.): VIII, 5, 137 (among the slain of Duryodhana's army).
Mālava^1 (“the king of the Mālavas”). § 591 (Saṃśaptakavadhap.): VII, 17, 691 (among the Saṃśaptakas). Cf. the two next.
Mālava^2 (do.) = Indravarman: VII, 8708 (Indravarmaṇah, of the Pāṇḍava army, his elephant named Aśvatthāman is slain by Bhīmasena), 8744 (do., do.), 8949 (do., do.).
Mālava^3 (do.) = Sudarśana: VII, 9330 (Sudarśanaḥ, attacked Aśvatthāman), 9334, †9337, 9343 (slain by Aśvatthāman), 9400 (Sudarśane…hate).
Mālavā, a river. § 775 (Ānuśāsanik.): XIII, 166, 7651 (enumeration).
Mallava, pl. (ºāḥ), a people. § 574 (Jambūkh.): VI, 9, 370 (only C., B. has Ballavāḥ).
Mālavānaka, pl. (ºāḥ), a people. § 574 (Jambūkh.): VI, 9, 367 (only C., B. has Mālavā narāḥ).

Mālavī, wife of the Madra king Aśvapati. § 545 (Pativratāmāhātmyap.): III, 293, 16637 (read so instead of Mānavī); 297, 16807 (Yama promised that M. should bear 100 Mālavas to Aśvapati); 299, 16914 (the 100 sons are born).

Malaya^1, a mountain. § 39 (Rāmaṇīyaka): I, 27, 1309 (vṛkshair Mºjaiḥ, i.e. sandal-trees, BR.).--§ 269 (Vaiśravaṇasabhāv.): II, 10, 412 (present in the palace of Kubera).-§ 295 (Dyūtap.): II, 52, 1892 (the Cola king and the Pāṇḍya king brought as tribute sandal juice from M. and sandal and aloe tree from Dardura).--§ 375 (Tīrthayātrāp.): III, 85, 8234 (on M. one should ascend the funeral pyre).-§ 459 (Mārkaṇḍeyas.): III, 188, 12920 (seen by Mārkaṇḍeya in the stomach of Nārāyaṇa).--§ 531 (Rāmopākhyānap.): III, 280, 16126 (śrīmān iva mahāśailo Mºo meghamālayā).-§ 534 (Hanūmatpratyāgamana): III, 282, 16239 (SahyaMºau Dardurañ ca mahāgiriṃ), 16240 (crossed by the monkeys on their way to Laṅkā).--§ 548 (Āraṇeyap.): III, 313, †17318 (four mountains enumerated).--§ 555 (Indravijaya): V, 11, 353.--§ 574 (Jambūkh.): VI, 6, 252 (ºparvataḥ); 9, 318 (among the kulaparvatāḥ of Bhāratavarsha).--§ 594 (Mṛtyu): VII, 54, 2098 (Mṛtyu performed austerities on M.).--§ 603d (Tripura): VII, 202, 9564 (Śiva made M. the yūpa (i.e. yuga [yoke], Nīl.) of his chariot).--§ 605b (Pāṇḍya): VIII, 20, 803 (ºpratimaṃ, sc. the standard of the Pāṇḍya king (Malayadhvaja)).--§ 716 (Śukābhipatana): XII, 333, 12597 (parvataṃ, there Urvaśī and Pūrvacitti always dwell).--§ 775 (Ānuśāsanik.): XIII, 166, 7657 (enumeration).
Malaya^2, a mountain in Śākadvīpa. § 575b (Śākadvīpa): VI, 11, 416 (parvataḥ). Cf. Jalada.
Malaya^3, a Suparṇa, son of Garuḍa. § 564 (Mātalīyop.): V, 101, 3599 (only C., B. has Māº).
Malaya, pl. (ºāḥ), a people. § 574 (Jambūkh.): VI, 9, 353 (only C., B. has Malajāḥ).
Mālaya, v. Malaya^3.
Malayadhvaja, name of a Pāṇḍya king. § 605 (Karṇap.): VIII, 20, 789, †809 (slain by Aśvatthāman). Cf. Pāṇḍya.
Mālin = Śiva (1000 names^2).
Mālinī^1, a river. § 133 (Dushyanta): I, 70, 2864 (flowed by the hermitage of Kaṇva), 2872.--§ 134 (Viśvāmitra): I, 72, 2946 (prasthe Himavato ramye Mºīm abhito nadīṃ, there Menakā bore Śakuntalā).
Mālinī^2, one of the mothers of Śiśu. § 500 (Skandop.): III, 228, 14396.
Mālinī^3, a Rākshasī. § 526 (Rāmopākhyānap.): III, 275, 15893, 15896 (by Viśravas, mother of Vibhīshaṇa).
Mālinī^4, a goddess. § 549 (Pāṇḍavapraveśap.): IV, 9, 259 (Draupadī is asked if she is M.).
Mālinī^5, § 549 (Pāṇḍavapraveśap.): IV, 9, 264 (the name which Draupadī assumed at the court of Virāṭa).
Mālinī^6, a city (according to Harivaṃca, v. 1699, identical with Campā). § 621 (Rājadh.): XII, 5, 134 (given to Karṇa by Jarāsandha).
Mallarāshṭra (“the kingdom of the Mallas”). § 574 (Jambūkh.): VI, 9, 352. Cf. Malla, pl.
Mālyapiṇḍaka, a serpent. § 564 (Mātalīyop.): V, 103, 3629 (enumeration).

Mālyavat, one or more mountains. § 436 (Yakshayuddhap.): III, 158, 11560 (mahāgiriṃ, in the north, passed by by the Pāṇḍavas on their way to Gandhamādana).--§ 531 (Rāmopākhyānap.): III, 280, 16118 (ºo 'bhyāse, the abode of Sugrīva, in the south), 16132 (pṛshṭhe Mºaḥ, there Rāma dwelt for four months).--§ 534 (Hanūmatpratyāgamana): III, 282, 16197, 16218.--§ 574 (Jambūkh.): VI, 6, 203 (south of Nīla and north of Nishadha); 7, 253 (parvataṃ). --§ 574j (do.): On the summit of M. is always seen the fire called Saṃvartaka, which blazes forth at the end of the yuga for the destruction of the universe. On the summit of M. towards the east there are many small mountains; M. measures 11,000 yojanas. The men there are of the complexion of gold; they have fallen from the Brahmaloka and are good, and given to severe ascetic austerities and sexual abstinence (ūrdhvaretasaḥ); in order to protect the creatures they enter the sun; heated with the sun's rays for 66,000 years, they then enter the lunar disc: VI, 7, 281, 282.-§ 782g (Guruśishyasaṃv.): XIV, 43, 1174.
